clue.text: Sailor joining vessel gets top prize

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is an old name for a sailor
a pot is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A seaman boarding a ship lands the biggest reward going.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the largest prize in a lottery or gaming machine, the top award on offer.

clue.text: Judge initially terribly proud about hospital in Indian city

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of judge
about means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the hospital letter
terribly signals the letters of proud are put in a bad, jumbled order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A judge, terribly proud, visits a hospital in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns PROUD into ODPUR, and 'about' puts it round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Jodhpur is a city in Rajasthan in India, which gave its name to riding breeches.

clue.text: Run after mate one's located between decks

indicators.note: after means the first piece named follows the second

parts.note: a mate is a companion
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying after a friend who is somewhere between a ship's decks.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is the British term for a run in stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion ladder is the stairway on a ship leading from one deck to another.

clue.text: Model that's changed inside very quickly

indicators.note: inside means the rearranged letters are put within the outer word

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters of that's are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A model whose look has changed inside in a great hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an adverb meaning with great speed, from the old haste of postal riders.

clue.text: Suddenly sees divining rods?

definitions.meaning: in British slang to twig is to grasp or realise all at once
dowsers traditionally use forked sticks to search for water

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to catch on; the noun sense is small branches, the kind cut for dowsing.

clue.text: Splendid member, one in the field?

parts.note: fine means splendid or excellent
a leg is a limb, one of the body's members

explanation.surface: A splendid limb, perhaps belonging to a player out on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: FINE LEG is a fielding position in cricket, behind the batsman on the leg side; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine leg names a cricket fielder's position, so the person stationed there is one out on the field.

clue.text: Angler is on Channel Island filling cooler

indicators.note: filling means the pieces go inside the outer word

parts.note: a fan is a cooler

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the following piece

parts.note: Herm is one of the small Channel Islands, near Guernsey

explanation.surface: A fisherman on a Channel Island loads up his cool box.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is a small island in the Channel Islands between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes with rod and line, so is a kind of fisherman.

clue.text: Sound of organ I installed

indicators.note: installed means set within, so the letter goes inside the body part

parts.note: the nose is the organ of smell

explanation.surface: The sound coming from a church organ I have put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, especially a loud or unwelcome one.

clue.text: Taffy's her old man, playing a patriotic song

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the phrase are played with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Welshman is her dad, performing a patriotic anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: Taffy is old slang for a Welshman, and the answer is the Welsh national anthem, so the surface fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Land of My Fathers is the English title of Hen Wlad Fy Nhadau, the national anthem of Wales.

clue.text: Most white, egrets flying across end of estuary

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters stretch over and around the other letter
flying suggests the letters of egrets scatter into a new arrangement
end of means take the final letter of estuary

explanation.surface: White egrets fly across the mouth of an estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' turns EGRETS into GREEST, which goes 'across' the Y from 'end of estuary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes hair turned white with age, so the most grey-haired is the whitest.

clue.text: Household skills of servants around disturbed niece

parts.note: domestics are household servants
C stands for circa, Latin for around

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters of niece are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: The household staff are rattled by an unsettled niece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but here gives C, for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic science is the old school subject teaching cookery, cleaning and running a home: household skills.

clue.text: Start to pick every single fruit

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter, taken here from pick

parts.note: every single one is each one

explanation.surface: An orchard instruction: begin harvesting each and every piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is a soft, downy stone fruit, one example of a fruit.

clue.text: Docker set off, drove erratically close to edge

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of place, so the letters of set are rearranged
erratically means without order, so the letters of drove are shuffled
the close to a word is its final letter, here from edge

explanation.surface: A dock worker sets out and drives wildly near the edge of the quay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' looks like a verb phrase for departing, but 'off' scrambles the word before it, just as 'erratically' does.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a person employed to load and unload ships, a docker.

clue.text: Sudden mental aberration losing head in squall

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden fit of confusion or mental disturbance

explanation.surface: Someone has a sudden mental lapse while caught in a squall.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAINSTORM is the unstated word, 'losing head' takes off its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A squall is a sudden violent gust of wind often bringing heavy rain, much like a rainstorm.

clue.text: Partner's second and last drink?

definitions.meaning: a spouse or partner, often called one's better half
a final half-pint ordered after the first, before leaving the pub

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jokey term for one's spouse, and also an invitation to one more half-pint before closing.

clue.text: Forward terms of reference

definitions.meaning: to forward is to send on, as one sends money or a case to another body
the scope of authority or task given to a person or committee

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means send or pass on; as a noun it means the set brief within which someone works.

clue.text: Palatable stuff provided by lyricist daily

parts.note: Tim Rice is the lyricist of Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar
a daily is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: Tasty material supplied by a songwriter in the daily press.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice paper is an edible sheet used under macaroons and in Asian cooking, so stuff fit to eat.

clue.text: Spread of craze to cover North

indicators.note: to cover something is to go over it, so the outer word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a rage is a craze or fad, the rage of the moment
N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A fashion that spreads until it covers the north of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is the extent or spread of something, as in a range of prices.

clue.text: Let back in on a date briefly with German

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
D is the abbreviation for date
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A German is allowed back in after a brief date.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit someone is to admit them again, letting them back inside.

clue.text: Restrains manual workers holding strike

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the second inside it

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farm hands
to cuff is to strike with an open hand

explanation.surface: Workers on strike are held back by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs are the linked metal rings police use to restrain a prisoner's wrists; here a noun.

clue.text: Pastry ruled out after stone put on

indicators.note: after says the jumbled letters come behind the abbreviation

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of ruled are put out of order

explanation.surface: A pastry is banned once someone has gained a stone in weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns RULED into RUDEL; a stone is a British unit of body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a layered Austrian pastry, typically filled with apple.

clue.text: Evergreen song about gold vehicle

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the song's letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An evergreen hit song tells of a golden car.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria is the monkey puzzle tree; 'Evergreen' looks like a description of the song but is the definition. The name was also a famous Guardian setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the genus of conifers including the monkey puzzle, trees that keep their leaves all year.

clue.text: In small room, old musical instrument

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: An old instrument kept in a tiny room.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument played between the knees.

clue.text: Bowl in field trapping last of batsmen

indicators.note: trapping means the outer word catches the letter inside it

parts.note: an area is a field, as in a field of study

indicators.note: last of means take the final letter of batsmen

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler in the field traps the last of the batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' looks like a cricket verb but is the noun for a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl is a stadium with tiered seating around it, as an arena is.

clue.text: Father right next to the head

indicators.note: next to means the first piece is placed alongside the other one

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: Dad's position is right beside the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father and old British schoolboy slang for one's dad.

clue.text: A sign of growing older: forgotten times and pressure to study

parts.note: the Middle Ages are a long-gone historical era, times largely forgotten
P is the physics symbol for pressure
to read is to study, as in reading law

explanation.surface: Getting older shows when old times fade from memory under pressure to keep studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-age spread is the extra weight round the waist that tends to come with getting older.

clue.text: Bore, upper-class type describing vase

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the outer word encircles the other piece

parts.note: a toff is British slang for a posh, upper-class person
an urn is a large vase

explanation.surface: A posh dullard droning on about an ornamental vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense, to trace a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn-off is something that kills interest, so a bore in the sense of a tedious thing.

clue.text: Spray article — could be looser afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards places the following piece behind the first one

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: could be says the letters of looser may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A product advert: spray this item and it might loosen up later.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a can that releases its contents as a fine mist, a spray.
